title: Your Life As a Lighthouse Keeper

lines.text: It's eighteen ninety-one. You are a lighthouse keeper.
Your whole world is one rock, one tower, and one light that must never go out.
You wake at four, before the sun, because the lamp needs you.
A hundred and twelve steps. Every morning. Every night.
You polish the great lens until it gleams, and trim the wick so the flame burns clean.
Every few hours, you write it all down. The wind. The weather. Every ship that passes.
Once a month, a boat brings supplies.
If the sea is rough, it doesn't come at all.
So you eat what you stored. Salted fish. Hard bread. Tea, again.
Some nights, the storm is so loud you can't hear yourself think.
Then you see it. A ship, far too close to the rocks.
You keep the light turning. And you wait.
By morning, the sea is calm. The ship is gone. Safe.
Nobody will ever thank you. Most people will never even know your name.
